text:
maya_sales: hey team — quick question from Acme SOC/procurement. For their air-gapped POC they want our recommended transport and validation flow. options they asked about: USB courier vs disk courier vs onsite transfer, max bundle size, signing & SBOM, and expected upgrade cadence. any hard blockers or cost notes we should call out?

ravi_se: short answer: we do signed offline bundles + manifest. typical pattern is base image + delta chunks. base can be big, deltas small. recommend encrypted courier for < 10GB, disk courier (shipped HDD) for > 10GB, or staged multi-part USB if they require. avoid relying on presigned S3 for fully air-gapped.

ravi_se: packaging notes: we produce a tar.gz with manifest.json, sbom.json, and sigs (cosign style). we also provide a verification script they run locally. no internet required.

ravi_se: example verify snippet we send customers:
```
# verify signature + checksum
cosign verify-blob --key <pubkey.pem> ./bundle.tar.gz.sig || exit 1
sha256sum -c manifest.json
```

maya_sales: good. what's the engineering effort and any licensing caveats? they want a ballpark to include in SOW.

taylor_eng: effort depends on model artifacts + quantization bundles. ballpark: prep + validation for a single POC bundle ~ 6-12 engineer hours (create bundle, SBOM, signature, QA). if we need custom chunking or bespoke install hooks add 4-8h. for recurring monthly delta bundles add ongoing ~2-4h/month.

taylor_eng: constraints:
- we can support automatic delta generation only if model files follow our artifact layout; otherwise manual.
- max single-file chunk handling: our installer expects pieces <= 16GB. larger than that needs disk courier.
- HSM-backed signing: supported for enterprise but needs key provisioning and SLA (extra ops coordination).

maya_sales: and pricing for courier costs? customer asked whether we cover shipping vs they cover.

ravi_se: we don't include shipping in standard terms. typical approach: customer covers physical shipping. if they want us to handle logistics, we add a pass-through + 4% handling. mention in SOW: "Customer pays shipping; Redwood can manage at cost + fee".

maya_sales: security questionnaire stuff — will SBOM + cosign be enough for their infosec? they flagged requirement for reproducible provenance and signed supply chain.

taylor_eng: SBOM + signed manifest + file checksums covers most requests. for stricter audits we can produce a build provenance file (gzipped) showing commit hashes and builder image ID. cosign + Rekor entries available on request.

certs_ops_bot: bundle-1776543210: signed by redwood-ops (cosign) sha256: abcdef123456... (truncated)

maya_sales: perfect. anything else to flag for timeline/upgrade cadence? customer initially said they only allow quarterly maintenance windows.

ravi_se: quarterly windows are fine. we recommend planning: full base deploy during a window, apply 1-2 delta patches between windows only for critical fixes. automatic fallback/rollback is supported but needs canary testing; include a canary plan in SOW.

taylor_eng: rollback note: offline rollback requires keeping previous bundle snapshot onsite or requesting a recovery bundle. advise customer to store the last two bundles on local storage.

maya_sales: awesome — I'll compile this into a short SOW blurb and pricing note. thanks :thumbsup:

ravi_se: np. ping if they ask for any custom signing (HSM) or an installer tweak.

taylor_eng: ack.

maya_sales: looping in legal for SOW language and ops for any hand-carrying fees.

maya_sales: (to customer) sending this summary now — will follow up with SOW + estimated timing and shipping options.
